question: Why do we keep our feet apart when lifting a patient?

options.A: To speed up the speed of the patient transfer
options.B: To increase overall physical stability and balance
options.C: To maximize the strength of upper arm muscles
options.D: To reduce the total body weight of the patient

explanation: Keeping your feet apart widens your base of support, lowering your center of gravity so you won't easily lose your balance while lifting. You've got this! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why should a midwife avoid twisting the body while lifting something heavy?

options.A: It places too much strain on the lower back discs
options.B: It immediately reduces the blood supply to the lower extremities
options.C: It activates the abdominal muscles too quickly for safe breathing
options.D: It causes the center of gravity to shift upward toward the chest

explanation: Twisting while bearing weight puts heavy, uneven pressure on your lower back. Protecting your spine keeps you strong and pain-free for your shifts! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the very first thing a midwife should check before trying to lift a patient from a bed?

options.A: Call for at least two other nurses to help
options.B: Raise the bed to the highest possible level
options.C: Assess the patient's weight and mobility status
options.D: Lock the wheels of the wheelchair immediately

explanation: Always check what the patient can do for themselves first! It saves your energy and helps you choose the safest way to help them. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h2)

question: A new mother who had an epidural wants to get out of bed to use the toilet. What is the safest first step for the midwife?

options.A: Ask her to stand up quickly so the medication does not make her dizzy
options.B: Encourage her to walk alone since postpartum women recover very fast
options.C: Lift her entirely by yourself without checking her balance first
options.D: Check her leg strength and feeling before moving her

explanation: Epidurals can leave legs temporarily weak or numb. Always test her leg control first to prevent a nasty fall! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why is it important to stand as close as possible to the patient when helping them move?

options.A: To prevent the patient from falling backward onto the mattress
options.B: To minimize the leverage distance and reduce strain on the back
options.C: To ensure the patient feels comforted by close physical contact
options.D: To make it easier to whisper instructions into the patient's ear

explanation: Holding the patient close to your own center of gravity makes them feel much lighter and protects your back muscles from strain. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why must you lock the wheels of both the bed and the stretcher before moving a patient between them?

options.A: To prevent the surfaces from separating and causing the patient to fall
options.B: To comply with hospital administrative regulations regarding fire exits
options.C: To keep the electronic mattress inflation system from shutting down
options.D: To ensure the bedding stays clean and free from floor dust

explanation: Unsecured beds can drift apart mid-move, leaving a dangerous gap. Locking the wheels keeps everything steady and secure! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which assistive device is primarily used to reduce friction when sliding a patient laterally across a bed?
explanation: Slide sheets feature a slippery surface that slides against itself, cutting down the physical effort needed to reposition a patient sideways. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h4)

question: A heavy, bedridden pregnant patient needs to be moved from a stretcher to the delivery bed. What is the safest equipment choice?

options.A: Manual lifting by at least four strong midwives pulling arms
options.B: A standard gait belt combined with gentle pulling by one nurse
options.C: Asking the patient to jump across the gap while holding rails
options.D: A mechanical overhead lift or specialized transfer mattress

explanation: For heavy or immobile patients, always use mechanical aids or slide equipment to keep both you and the patient safe from injury. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the main job of the leader during a team patient lift?

options.A: To lift the heaviest part of the patient's body alone
options.B: To count out loud and coordinate the timing of the movement
options.C: To push the wheelchair from behind while others lift
options.D: To document the transfer in the patient's nursing notes

explanation: One clear voice counting down ensures everyone moves at the exact same second, preventing sudden strain or dropped loads. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is counting out loud together so important when lifting with a partner?

options.A: It helps calm an anxious patient down during the physical transfer
options.B: It allows the hospital supervisor to monitor staff productivity
options.C: It speeds up the overall time required to complete the hospital shift
options.D: It prevents one person from taking unexpected weight before they are ready

explanation: Teamwork is all about timing! A good countdown means nobody takes the strain alone or gets caught off guard. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which part of the body do healthcare workers hurt most often when they lift incorrectly?
explanation: The lower back takes the hardest hit during improper lifting. Learning proper ergonomics is a huge superpower for your nursing career! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the most effective way for a hospital to lower the rate of lifting injuries among midwives?

options.A: Reduce the number of patients admitted to the maternity ward daily
options.B: Provide proper training and mechanical lifting equipment
options.C: Require all midwives to perform physical stretching exercises only at home
options.D: Punish staff members who report minor back pain after a shift

explanation: Good hospitals protect their staff by providing the right tools and training, making heavy lifting much safer for everyone. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h6)
